criticality.title: Critical dependency hierarchy
criticality.lead: Foundational infrastructure and shared state are shown before applications, using declared required dependencies and their transitive blast radius.

tierDescriptions.foundation: Network, storage and container foundations whose failure can remove whole layers of the homelab.
tierDescriptions.shared-data: Databases, caches and storage backends required by one or more higher-level services.
tierDescriptions.shared-platform: Gateways, runtimes and shared capabilities consumed transitively by applications.
tierDescriptions.application: User-facing or workflow services that consume the shared foundations above.
tierDescriptions.support: Optional, observability or inventory components with no declared blocking blast radius.

criticality.note: Criticality is derived from blocking required relations (dependsOn, consumesApi, routesTo, storesIn, authenticatesVia and structural partOf). Databases, caches and storage kinds are treated as shared state when they have required dependents. Observability and exposure links do not artificially increase startup criticality.

dns.title: DNS resilience
dns.independent: pfSense / Unbound keeps a resolution path independent from TrueNAS.
dns.truenasOnly: pfSense DNS forwarding depends only on TrueNAS-hosted DNS; a TrueNAS outage can become a LAN-wide DNS outage.
dns.resolverFailed: pfSense DNS Resolver is disabled or not running.
dns.unconfigured: pfSense DNS observation is not configured; independence from TrueNAS is not verified.
dns.unreachable: The pfSense DNS control-plane observation is unavailable; service health alone does not prove DNS resilience.
dns.incomplete: pfSense DNS is observable but resilience evidence is incomplete.
dns.upstreamCount: {count, plural, =0 {no configured upstream} one {# configured upstream} other {# configured upstreams}}
dns.snapshotStale: The displayed posture comes from the last valid snapshot because the live health refresh failed.
dns.evidenceNote: Control-plane policy evidence only; this is not a synthetic DNS query from a LAN client.
